learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge and understanding of engineering disciplines specific to their specialty, at the level necessary to acquire the rest of the degree competencies, including notions of the latest advances.
Be aware of the multidisciplinary context of engineering.

Engineering analysis: The ability to analyze complex products, processes, and systems in their field of study; to choose and apply established analytical, calculation, and experimental methods appropriately and to correctly interpret the results of such analyses.

Engineering analysis: The ability to identify, formulate and solve engineering problems in their specialty; to choose and apply established analytical, calculation and experimental methods appropriately; to recognize the importance of social, health and safety, environmental, economic and industrial constraints.

Engineering projects: Ability to design, plan and develop complex products (parts, components, finished products, etc.), processes and systems in their specialty, which comply with established requirements, including being aware of social, health and safety, environmental, economic and industrial aspects; as well as selecting and applying appropriate project methods.
Practical application of engineering: Understanding of applicable techniques and methods of analysis, project, and research and their limitations in their field of expertise.
Practical application of engineering: Knowledge of the social, health and safety, environmental, economic and industrial implications of engineering practice.

Practical application of engineering: General ideas about economic, organizational and management issues (such as project management, risk and change management) in an industrial and business context.
Judgment formation: Ability to manage complex technical or professional activities or projects in their specialty, taking responsibility for decision-making.
Communication and Teamwork: Ability to effectively communicate information, ideas, problems and solutions in the field of engineering and with society in general.
Communication and Teamwork: Ability to function effectively in national and international contexts, individually and in teams, and to cooperate with both engineers and people from other disciplines.
Design a workspace related to lean production.

teaching_methods: Development, writing, and presentation of reports, memos, and audiovisual material related to projects/POPBLs (individual or in teams)
Individual study and work, tests, exams, and/or control points
Lectures and participatory classes by the professor on concepts and procedures
Exercises and practical assignments (individual and team)

assessment_methods.method: Written and oral individual tests for the evaluation of technical competencies
Technical capacity, involvement in the project/PBL, work performed, results obtained, delivered documentation, technical presentation and defense
Observation of student participation and attitude in the proposed formative activities

assessment_rules: Assessment is structured by specific competencies/learning outcomes (e.g., RG202, RGM235), with different weighting schemes for each. For some competencies, individual written and oral tests constitute a portion (e.g., 55.4% or 62%), while project-based work and observation of participation account for the remainder. For other competencies, project-based work, including documentation and defense, accounts for 100% of the evaluation. For project-based assessments, continuous evaluation is conducted through team meetings with tutors and experts; corrections applied to the final version of the project report are considered the recovery mechanism. For written/oral tests, mechanisms for recovery are sometimes stated as repeating the test, but in other cases, no mechanisms are explicitly provided.
